ranking_metric: Debian popcon installations (sourcemax/by_inst), maximum over binary packages of the source package
selection: Highest popcon count among C++ JSON parser source packages in the 'json' source-name search: libjsoncpp (JsonCpp) 32,707, also highest at dev-package level (libjsoncpp-dev 2,203 vs nlohmann-json3-dev 1,799). C libraries in the same search (json-c, JSON-GLib, cJSON and libfastjson above it; yyjson below) are excluded from the C++ cell. Second selected path: nlohmann/json 3.12.0 (nlohmann-json3 source 1,799; nlohmann-json3-dev 1,799), the highest-adoption C++ JSON library by GitHub stars (50,894, secondary signal) and the highest dev-package popcon count after libjsoncpp-dev among non-framework C++ JSON libraries. simdjson's source count (2,688) is higher but comes from its runtime library; its dev package has 36 installs.
uncertainty: Pilot cell: JsonCpp 1.9.8 and nlohmann/json 3.12.0 were built and control-verified. Popcon measures Debian installs; JsonCpp's runtime count is inflated by dependents such as CMake, and header-only libraries (nlohmann/json, RapidJSON) have only dev packages, so popcon undercounts them. GitHub stars rank nlohmann/json first (50,894 vs 8,916). simdjson is above nlohmann/json at popcon source level (2,688 vs 1,799) through its runtime library but was not built. Eight leads are logged in leads.json and are not selected or ranked. Framework packages (Qt, Boost, POCO) are not ranked by whole-framework installs. The ISO C++ standard library has no JSON API. Two valid controls do not establish complete RFC 8259 support.
